U03-ADJ-USE.evidence_note: Strong/weak conditions and agreement. Cook says weak sometimes after possessives; this is not a universal possessive→weak rule.

U03-STRONG.evidence_note: Complete strong pattern, short/long stems, æ/a alternation, disyllabic syncope and optional loss of -u, -e stems, h-loss and consonant simplification.

U03-WEAK.evidence_note: Complete weak pattern. Selected ordinary Gpl -ra; -a/-ena are explicitly admitted alternatives. Comparative Gpl contraction is explained, not a license to invent arbitrary assimilation.

U03-COMPARE.evidence_note: Regular, umlaut and irregular degrees; comparative weak, superlative usually weak. Selected representative series below, not blanket mastery of all examples.

U03-ADVERB.evidence_note: Adverb formation and degree; wīd→wīde, swīð→swīðe very, sōð→sōðlice truly. Adverbs modify verbs, adjectives or adverbs.

U03-NUMERAL.evidence_note: Cardinal/ordinal spellings and complete one/two/three rules; ordinals weak except ōðer.

U03-POSSESSIVE.evidence_note: Six agreeing first/second-person possessives; third-person genitives indeclinable. sīn not selected.

U03-DEMONSTRATIVE.evidence_note: Full that/this paradigms. Cook prints short-e ðes, not ðēs; selected double-s variants. Instrumental is reference recognition only.

U03-WRIGHT-USE.evidence_note: Positive/superlative predicate strong; eall and ōðer always strong. Full paradigms confirm agreement; mixed-gender predicate exception remains outside present tasks.

U03-WRIGHT-SYNCOPE.evidence_note: Long-disyllable syncope with retention before consonantal endings; analogical micles/miclum explicitly printed; hāligu and hālgu variants; -erra/-erre may simplify.

U03-WRIGHT-E.evidence_note: Full wilde pattern used by ūre, with its separate fem.Nsg exception in §464.

U03-WRIGHT-GEARU.evidence_note: Complete gearu strong pattern (gearone, gearore, gearora; gearw- before vowel) and weak gearwa/gearwe.

U03-WRIGHT-HEAH.evidence_note: Complete contracted hēah strong pattern and weak hēa, hēan. Selected hēanne/hēarre/hēarra/hēaum; source also gives simpler variants.

U03-WRIGHT-COMPARE.evidence_note: Comparatives weak; irregular series and their variants. Does not individually attest every derived case.

U03-WRIGHT-NUMERAL.evidence_note: Plural ān rare with different distributive sense, not cardinal one with plural count nouns; 4–19 generally uninflected before a noun, with separately conditioned inflection outside this unit.

U03-WRIGHT-POSSESSIVE.evidence_note: uncer/incer/ēower explicitly like hālig; ūre like wilde except F.Nsg ūre. ūrre/ūrra may simplify. Combined with §§429/431 yields transparent pattern-derived cells.

U03-WRIGHT-ADVERB.evidence_note: Exact wel/bet/betst and regular -or/-ost pattern; Cook hook spelling selected for bęt/bętst.

U03-THAN.evidence_note: Attested Beowulf469 comparison Sē wæs betere þonne iċ! provides a nominative standard after than with unexpressed repeated copula. Bounded analogous composition, not a claim that all than-constructions take nominative.
U03-THAN.edition: R. D. Fulk, An Introductory Grammar of Old English (2014), corrected open-access reprint, June 2020.
U03-THAN.source_attribution: Beo 469 in Fulk §35. Retain Fulk’s printed betere in this evidence quotation; it is not the selected masculine comparative model in the course.

features.description: A finite content clause introduced by invariant ðæt fills the content complement of the selected knowing/saying verb.
features.scope_note: Keep distinct from determiner/relative ðæt; clause has its own subject and finite verb.

features.description: Reported content commonly uses subjunctive; a proposition asserted as fact may use indicative.
features.scope_note: Exercises must name the communicative stance when a specific mood is required; subjunctive does not mean the report is false.

features.description: In a report, recover referents and the time of the reported situation from the stated context; adjust person accordingly.
features.scope_note: Limited simultaneous present/past reports only. No universal English-style backshift, automatic pronoun replacement, or systematic tense-sequence doctrine; advanced Unit12 scope remains deferred.

features.description: Wh question clauses can be complements of witan or sęcgan, including Saga mē + wh clause. The wh form takes its internal case.
features.scope_note: This is an embedded question, not an ordinary relative antecedent construction. Subjunctive is a normal selected reporting/question pattern; factual indicative is defensible in suitable context.

features.description: Invariant hwæðer introduces a dependent yes/no question after witan/sęcgan.
features.scope_note: Distinct lemma/sense from inflected hwæðer which of two. No direct-question use of the new conjunction is inferred.

features.description: Hātan command takes accusative actor + plain infinitive. The infinitive may retain its own accusative object.
features.scope_note: Select hātan for II.12.5; no unnecessary gebēodan system. Dative reporting addressee is a different function.

features.description: Gesēon can take an accusative actor and a plain infinitive describing the perceived action.
features.scope_note: The actor belongs to the infinitival event; no claim that every verb takes this construction.

features.description: Gewyrcean may take an accusative object and an agreeing accusative predicate adjective.
features.scope_note: Contrast prior hātan naming two-accusative construction; morphology must agree with the object, not the main subject.

features.description: Preterite subjunctive can express a wish contrary to the present situation, including Wǣre ic ...!
features.scope_note: Promotes bounded previously recognition-only nonpast unreal use. No general counterfactual conditional or pluperfect system.

features.description: Dative experiencer + lēofre is + plain infinitive expresses a preference; the comparison may contain parallel mid+dative phrases.
features.scope_note: Only this attested preference frame is productive; broad impersonal constructions are not inferred.

features.description: Sęcgan can name its recipient in the dative with direct speech or a dependent content/question complement.
Predicative headless ðæt means what/that which in be what one is/ought to be, without a separate expressed antecedent.
features.scope_note: Bounded identity/role pattern for II.11.5–6; not a general free-choice system or the statement conjunction.

features.description: A group may be named by personal genitive after substantival hwilc or sume; hīe sume is also Cook’s appositional some-of-them expression.
features.scope_note: Promote personal ēower only in this frame; prior hiera morphology is reused. No blanket personal-genitive syntax promotion.

features.description: Use on + accusative to locate an event on a numbered day.
features.scope_note: Prior supplied temporal sense promoted; this does not replace ordinary location on+dative.

features.description: Mid + dative names an accompanying person or cargo.
features.scope_note: Means/manner/abstract circumstance require their own prior or supplied records.

features.description: For-ðām introduces an indicative factual reason clause.
features.scope_note: Source spelling retained; no new consequence-purpose equivalence.

features.description: A predicate adjective referring jointly to subjects of different grammatical genders is normally neuterplural.
features.scope_note: II.9.6 has masculine ęle and neuter wīn; selected predicate is neuterplural gōd. Explain normal pattern without claiming exceptionless agreement.

features.description: Ne + willan expresses unwillingness/refusal; translate the sense from context.
features.scope_note: Use prior positive forms with ne; no additional negative contraction paradigm or future auxiliary system assigned.

features.description: Use prior tēon with accusative object plus forð to express produce/bring forth.
features.scope_note: Plain infinitive after hātan and hortative subjunctive use prior tēon forms; no new separable-prefix system taught.

features.description: Fręmman in the benefit sense governs the beneficiary in the dative.
Slēan may express making a stroke without naming an object.
features.scope_note: Bounded ordinary striking use for the hammer; prior accusative-object construction is not erased.

features.description: Complete present/preterite indicative systems of the seventeen explicitly selected new trade/narrative verbs.
features.scope_note: 204 cells. Citation infinitives do not license unassigned nonfinite production; wician plain infinitive is separately productive.

features.description: Complete singular/plural commands of rōwan, bycgan, sēcan, begān, gestillan and rǣdan.
features.scope_note: 12 cells; sēceað is a separately declared source recognition variant.

features.description: Complete present/preterite subjunctive of sēcan.
features.scope_note: 12 cells; present firstplural hortative required by II.9.12; no automatic teaching of every subordinate-clause use.

features.description: Recognize exact sēceað as the plural command variant of selected sēcað.
Behēfe useful takes a dative person to whom the subject is useful. The predicate adjective agrees with its subject, while the recipient noun is dative.
features.prior_status: The exact merchant clause was supplied in Unit8; ordinary productive useful+dative is new.

features.description: Use the nominative-shaped noun in direct address; an accompanying adjective is weak. Thus the morphology of the noun follows number and its own class, while good in O good fellows/workmen uses weak plural. Ēalā is an optional interjection where the original English says O.
features.prior_status: Only an exact merchant vocative was supplied in Unit8.

features.description: The bounded expression Godes ðēowdōm means service of God: God is the object of the service, not necessarily its agent or owner. Use ordinary genitive morphology with this explicitly taught lexical relationship.

Elpes bān means ivory, literally elephant’s bone. The whole expression is supplied for II.10.14: elpes is genitive singular, bān is neuter accusative singular as the thing sold. No rule forming arbitrary material names is inferred.
Āstīgan takes the ship as its direct accusative object in the selected go aboard/board sense. A separate mid+dative phrase names accompanying wares.

For II.12.7 supply libbende gesceafta, living creatures, feminine accusative plural. Libbende follows the documented feminine -e variant of the participial adjective; prior neuter libbendu is a different cell. The phrase is not independently recalled, and no full new libban participle system is assigned.

Productive manig means many as an ordinary attributive adjective agreeing with a plural noun. Its displayed singular cells are recognition reference only; singular many-a, substantival quantity and partitive constructions are outside this lexical scope.

For II.12.13 supply the complete phrase ðrēo hund and fīf and siextig daga, three hundred and sixty-five days. The hundred-unit is counted with neuter ðrēo; fīf and siextig gives five and sixty. Daga is genitive plural in the counted construction. This is a transparent local adaptation of Cook §§78–79, not a claim that Cook prints this exact 365 phrase or that all numerals beyond twelve are now productive.

To you it seems … to be / to me it seems … to hold. Treat these source expressions as whole supported frames. The person to whom it seems is dative. Cook explicitly labels furðra nominative singular; do not force the whole passage into a newly generalized accusative-and-infinitive rule. foremost; prior, weak comparative masculine nominative singular, exactly as Cook’s note14 identifies it. This one form/sense is supplied. Cook marks the is in each Teacher question and in swā-swā hit is gerǣd as conjectural, absent from his manuscripts. Preserve those editorial insertions with their note; the is in mē is geðūht belongs to a separate note15.
features.scope_note: Dative experiencer and source complementary infinitives; no claim that all source actors are accusative.

features.description: among these (occupations). Betweox and betweoh are the two exact spellings here; the following phrase is accusative plural. In the first question cræftas is understood after ðās.
features.scope_note: Exact bounded reading scaffold only; no unaided construction production follows.

features.description: just as it is read in the Gospel. Swā-swā means just as; gerǣd is the exact past participle used in this passive expression. This supplied phrase is not a new complete passive system. Cook marks the is in each Teacher question and in swā-swā hit is gerǣd as conjectural, absent from his manuscripts. Preserve those editorial insertions with their note; the is in mē is geðūht belongs to a separate note15.
features.scope_note: Exact bounded reading scaffold only; no unaided construction production follows.

features.description: all these things will be added to you. Eall agrees with neuter plural ðing. Bēoð is third-person plural here, and ēow is the dative recipient. Tōgēiecte is a source predicate participle: retain its -e under Cook’s explicit predicate-participle rule (§62), rather than changing it to a presumed neuter ending.
features.scope_note: Exact bounded reading scaffold only; no unaided construction production follows.

features.description: wise man; wise one, a direct address. This is the weak masculine singular of wīs used substantivally; its local personal use is supplied.
features.scope_note: Exact bounded reading scaffold only; no unaided construction production follows.

features.description: feeds us all. Ūs is accusative plural, ealle refers to the people fed (masculine plural), and fēt is present indicative third singular of fēdan. This exact verb form is supplied; the distinct productive āfēdan has its own full system.
features.scope_note: Exact bounded reading scaffold only; no unaided construction production follows.

features.description: God’s service, service of God; his righteousness. The genitives identify the divine possessor or object of service; his can follow its noun in the exact source. The service sense of ðēowdōm is new in this unit.
features.scope_note: Service of God has an objective genitive; ordinary possession alone does not silently establish this sense.

features.description: Complete selected sunu u-stem NGDA singular and plural. Sunu: N/A singular -u, G/D singular -a; N/G/A plural -a, D plural -um. The vowel is short. Cook records variation -u/-o outside genitives and dative plural, and later a-stem sunes/sunas. These are valid documented alternatives, not the selected target or an invitation to assign other u-stem lemmas.
features.scope_note: New complete noun-class assignment, including ordinary previously taught case uses; not the verbal participle system.

features.description: Complete selected rīce neuter -e NGDA singular and plural. Rīce has singular rīce/rīces/rīce/rīce and plural rīcu/rīca/rīcum/rīcu. The lexical -e disappears before the case ending. Cook explicitly allows inserted i/e in the plural after c/g: rīciu/rīcia etc.; these are valid unselected variants.
features.scope_note: New complete noun-class assignment, including ordinary previously taught case uses; not the verbal participle system.

features.description: Complete selected geðeahtend agent -end NGDA singular and plural. Geðeahtend follows the masculine -end agent-noun pattern, not the inflecting present participle. Selected singular geðeahtend/-es/-e/zero; plural N/A geðeahtend, G geðeahtendra, D geðeahtendum. N/A plural -e and rarer -as are documented alternatives.
features.scope_note: New complete noun-class assignment, including ordinary previously taught case uses; not the verbal participle system.

turns.text: Hwæt sægst ðū, wīsa? Hwilc cræft ðē is geðūht betweox ðās furðra wesan?

Ic sęcge ðē, mē is geðūht Godes ðēowdōm betweoh ðās cræftas ealdorscipe healdan, swā-swā hit is gerǣd on godspelle, “Fyrmest sēceað rīce Godes, and rihtwīsnesse his, and ðās ðing eall bēoð tōgēiecte ēow.”
And hwilc ðē is geðūht betweox woruldcræftas healdan ealdordōm?

local_support.anchor: swā-swā hit is gerǣd on godspelle

local_support.text: First seek (plural command). Sēceað is Cook’s exact source spelling; the selected productive plural command is sēcað. Retain and recognize this attested variant.

local_support.anchor: ðās ðing eall bēoð tōgēiecte ēow
local_support.text: all these things will be added to you. Eall agrees with neuter plural ðing. Bēoð is third-person plural here, and ēow is the dative recipient. Tōgēiecte is a source predicate participle: retain its -e under Cook’s explicit predicate-participle rule (§62), rather than changing it to a presumed neuter ending.

local_support.text: feeds us all. Ūs is accusative plural, ealle refers to the people fed (masculine plural), and fēt is present indicative third singular of fēdan. This exact verb form is supplied; the distinct productive āfēdan has its own full system.

limits: The actual eight active coverage contracts and cumulative registers are the sole prior-teaching authority. The archived course is evidence only; every Unit9 promotion retains its earlier supplied/recognition history.

Finite content clauses are productive after the selected knowing/saying frames only. Seeing receives the separately audited perception infinitive; no generalized seeing-content clause assignment is inferred.

Reported statements and dependent questions commonly select subjunctive in the stated settings. Contextual indicative can be valid; subjunctive does not assert falsity. Simultaneous present/past reports do not teach an automatic English backshift or the whole later tense/sequence system.
Inflected interrogative hwæðer and invariant whether hwæðer remain distinct lemmas and senses. Wh forms take their function's case inside the dependent clause.
Command hātan, perception gesēon and object-predicate gewyrcean each have a checked bounded lexical frame. Same-subject modal infinitives and naming hātan retain their distinct prior scopes.
The preterite subjunctive receives a bounded nonpast unreal-wish use. This does not teach general unreal conditionals or pluperfect constructions.

Only personal ēower in the assigned partitive frame is newly productive. Cook's hīe sume apposition is explained separately from a valid genitive alternative; other personal-genitive and indefinite systems remain limited.

The three new noun classes have literal complete NGDA tables. Other new nouns use complete earlier-class models plus explicit lexical stems and diagnostics. Every derivative cell is mapped, not falsely certified as printed verbatim.
Manig is productive as plural attributive many. Its singular forms and unassigned mass/abstract count-plurals remain recognition reference; displaying them creates no unassigned sense or syntax.

All17 selected new verb indicatives, six command pairs and sēcan subjunctives are complete. Other new infinitive citations remain supplied except the separately productive wician preference complement.
Sēceað is the exact source command variant, recognized with help. Sēcað is the selected productive plural command. Local fēt does not follow productively from prefixed āfēdan.

Supply the complete ivory, living-creatures and365-days phrases in their Cook tasks. The365 phrase is an explicit adaptation of numbered rules, not an exact source quotation or a complete higher-numeral system.

The source's seems frames, passives, among phrases, comparative furðra, substantival address and feeding phrase retain local support. Nominative hwilc/furðra must not be forced into the command/perception accusative-actor model.

All62 source words, four turns, thirteen notes and eleven help groups remain. The three conjectural is tokens and manuscript woruldcræftas note are explicit; nearby merchant/catalogue and smith passages remain unassigned.
Every public input and private required output is identified by actual form/sense IDs. Deliberately erroneous correction inputs are labeled and do not certify their syntax as good Old English.

audited_inflection_rules.rule: Sunu: N/A singular -u, G/D singular -a; N/G/A plural -a, D plural -um. The vowel is short. Cook records variation -u/-o outside genitives and dative plural, and later a-stem sunes/sunas. These are valid documented alternatives, not the selected target or an invitation to assign other u-stem lemmas.

Geðeahtend follows the masculine -end agent-noun pattern, not the inflecting present participle. Selected singular geðeahtend/-es/-e/zero; plural N/A geðeahtend, G geðeahtendra, D geðeahtendum. N/A plural -e and rarer -as are documented alternatives.

Rīce has singular rīce/rīces/rīce/rīce and plural rīcu/rīca/rīcum/rīcu. The lexical -e disappears before the case ending. Cook explicitly allows inserted i/e in the plural after c/g: rīciu/rīcia etc.; these are valid unselected variants.

Use explicit diagnostic stems: angel→angl-, fōdor→fōdr-, but ðyrel retains e. Cræft retains æ before its consonant cluster. Ealdormann follows mann in the final member: dat.sg and N/Apl ealdormęnn. Strong -e nouns replace final e before endings; -nes has -ness-. Smiððe/sīde are weak feminines; fyrspearca/trēowwyrhta/scēowyrhta/wyrhta/cęmpa weak masculines.

Behēfe is an -e adjective: replace lexical e with endings; selected strong feminine nominative singular and neuter N/A plural behēfu. Welig and manig retain medial i in the selected full paradigms and take -u in those cells (weligu/manigu). Wīs is heavy and lacks -u there. Wīsra adds comparative -r- without umlaut and declines weakly; genitive plural wīsra reduces doubled r beside s under Wright §259.3, as earlier lēofra does beside f. Strong feminine N/A plural -e is valid alongside selected -a; other variant cells require their own cited evidence rather than free analogical substitution. Manig is productive only as ordinary plural attributive many; its singular cells are recognition reference, without assigning many-a or substantival/partitive quantity constructions.

Mass/abstract unassigned plural senses remain outside independent production even though complete formal number paradigms are recorded. Hlæst wares and bęlg bellows are selected as plural; singular counterparts are recognition reference and do not add an unassigned singular sense. No source-supplied history is erased by a new production milestone.

audited_inflection_rules.statement: Each new verb has twelve explicit indicative cells, not just diagnostic principal parts. Present plurals share one form; preterite plurals share one form. Weak2sg past adds -st to the selected past1sg; strong2sg past takes the plural stem plus -e.

Cīepan takes -pte, āfēdan and selected weak rǣdan -dde; gestillan loses one l before -de; ālīehtan takes -hte with the two t sounds contracted. Bycgan/sēcan must learn bohte/sōhte. Fręmman retains doubled mm in most present forms but has fręmest/fręmeð and fręmede.

Select uncontracted present ālīehtest/ālīehteð to show the ending after the ht cluster. Present1sg ālīehte and past1/3sg ālīehte coincide; present2sg ālīehtest and past2sg ālīehtest coincide. No invented distinction from vowel length.

Rōwan changes ō→ē only in present2/3sg and has rēow past; blāwan ā→ǣ and blēow; bēatan ēa→īe and bēot; forlǣtan has forlēt; āstīgan has āstāg/āstige/āstigon. Final d/t + ð yields tt; g before st/ð yields h.
Prefixed begān follows gān throughout: begā/begǣst/begǣð/begāð; beēode/beēodest/beēodon. The prefix does not make the verb weak.
Wician, ðolian and gegaderian follow prior weakII: -ie/-ast/-að/-iað and -ode/-odest/-odon. Full new cells are displayed, though the class rules are prior.

Selected singular commands are rōw, byge, sēc, begā, gestil, rǣd; plural commands are the respective presentplural forms. Sēcan subjunctive uses sēce/sēcen and sōhte/sōhten. Source sēceað is preserved.

Full indicative display teaches indicative morphology only. Only six command pairs and the sēcan subjunctive are added. New citation infinitives are supplied except productive wician; source-only fēt, geðūht, gerǣd, tōgēiecte and libbende gesceafta remain locally supported. No systematic perfect, progressive, impersonal, infinitive tense or advanced sequence-of-tenses system follows.

Rǣdan is classified as usually weak in Cook§110 and explicitly as113 in his vocabulary: select rǣdde/rǣddon. Strong rēd/rēdon is a valid alternative system, not an independently required recall target.

Keep Cook hooked ę and macrons; selected bycgan/sēcan omit optional e before a vowel as Cook permits. BT bygeþ→bygeð is declared dental-letter normalization, with all quantities checked against Cook. Complete derived tables are new teaching material, not quoted historical paradigms.
